content.title: Flexbox: Put Items Into One Flow
content.hook: You have learned normal flow. Now meet a layout tool built for arranging a group of related items along one main direction: **Flexbox**.
content.context:
The core idea is simple:

**The parent becomes the flex container. Its direct children become flex items.**
goals: Use Flexbox for a one-dimensional row or column of related items and understand that the parent controls the layout relationship.

content.title: First example

content.question: You have three buttons inside `.toolbar`. After `display: flex`, what is the first useful expectation?

options.text: The children can participate in a shared flex layout.
Every child is placed at a random position.

feedback.correct: The important change is the relationship. The parent now establishes a flex layout for its direct children.
feedback.incorrect: The important change is the relationship. The parent now establishes a flex layout for its direct children.

content.question: Where does the rule that creates the flex layout go?

options.text: On the parent container that holds the items.
On the page's outermost element every time.

feedback.correct: `display: flex` creates the flex container. The direct children become flex items because of that parent relationship.
feedback.incorrect: `display: flex` creates the flex container. The direct children become flex items because of that parent relationship.

content.question:
You have three related controls that should sit in one horizontal group.

Which tool is designed for this relationship?

options.text: Rewriting the controls as one image
Adding random offsets to each control
Changing the meaning of the controls

feedback.correct: Flexbox is designed for a shared one-dimensional relationship between related items.

content.question:

feedback.correct: The useful beginner model is relationship-first: Flexbox arranges related items along a main axis.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Flexbox is a parent-controlled relationship among direct children.
**Senior habit:** Choose a layout tool because of the relationship you need, not because a snippet is popular.
**Mastery signal:** You can look at a group of sibling elements and explain why turning their parent into a flex container changes the relationship.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
